_about: The phases of forge, read by gate.py. modes: the phases of each mode, in order. optional: may be skipped with the user's reason (motion only while the look level is 1: from level 2 it builds the level, rules.md section 10, and launch's checks count it); secure never. added: newer than some projects, so a state from before them records neither and is not damaged. asks: auto mode never records these, the go is the user's own each time. parts: the skill that holds each phase as a part (its steps are in ../forge-<skill>/steps/<phase>.md); a phase that is not listed is a skill of its own, forge-<phase>. skip_only: an optional phase that skip refuses while look level 2 or higher is on record (forge-work/levels.json), or while level.py cannot read the record (a damaged or linked levels.json), with the words status and the next step add to it. steps: what gate.py prints: the next step ({0} the phase, {1} the gate's own command, {2} its skill, {3} its skip_only words), the line init adds, and the refusals of a held skip (held: {0} the look level; unread: {0} what level.py said).

steps.plain: Next: {0}. Run /{2}, then {1} check {0}. Show the user the skill's checkpoint plus one line with the gate result, and wait for their go. Then: {1} done {0} --approved '<their exact words>'
steps.auto: Next: {0}. Auto mode, if the user turned it on in this chat (a new chat asks again): run /{2}, fix what fails, stop where rules.md 7 says (the concept pick, the app's name, a Verdict: FAIL), give the checkpoint as a report, then {1} done {0} --auto '<their words>'
steps.skip: . Or, when the user says so{3}: {1} skip {0} --reason '<their reason>'
steps.done: All phases are done. Tell the user what they have now, what is left, and that shipping is their step.
steps.init: Auto mode, when the user asked for it in this chat: once check passes, done --auto '<their words>', the checkpoint as a report, and go on (rules.md 7).
steps.held: look level {0} is on record, and from level 2 motion builds the level: it is not skipped, in auto mode too (rules.md section 10). Wanted out: tell the user the app then stays near level 1; with their yes, first level.py set look 1 --said '<their words>'.
steps.unread: level.py get look cannot read the look level, so motion is not skipped (rules.md section 10). Show the user what it says, and change nothing yourself: {0}
